title: Z.ai GLM 4.6: What We Learned From 100 Million Open Source Downloads — Yuxuan Zhang, Z.ai
talk_summary: A Z.ai researcher presents GLM 4.6/4.5 model training details: data curriculum, RL framework (slime) with coupled/decoupled modes, token-weighted loss, and multimodal input handling. It is mostly a model-release marketing/training talk, but a few training-data and RL design mechanisms hint at how to structure agent tasks and evals.

takeaways.technique: Agent-style coding benchmark from real trajectories
takeaways.what_they_do: They built CC-Bench on top of Claude Code with 74 real agent coding tasks (frontend, internal tools, data analysis, algorithms) and record the full agent trajectory: query, planning, tool calls, code edits, execution.
takeaways.evidence_quote: for every model we record the full agent trader query the planning st the call and code adds and execution
takeaways.numbers: 74 tasks; GLM 4.6 ~68.6% win rate vs Claude 4

takeaways.what_they_do: They pack multi-file issues, PRs, and diffs from the same project into one long context so the model learns cross-file chains and real project structure end-to-end, extending context to 32k then 128k-200k.
takeaways.evidence_quote: packed into one long contains and the goal is to teach the model to following the close file and understand the chains

takeaways.technique: Decoupled async rollout for slow agent tasks
takeaways.what_they_do: For agent tasks with slow external steps (browser, backend API), they decouple rollout workers from training: workers talk to real environments and write trajectories to a shared buffer, training consumes at its own pace and periodically pushes new weights, so slow tasks don't block the pipeline.
takeaways.evidence_quote: even if some tasks super slow they don't block the whole training pipeline

takeaways.technique: Token-weighted loss to avoid short template answers
takeaways.what_they_do: They average loss over tokens instead of sequences during code RL, which reduces the incentive to emit very short template answers just to collect reward.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it reduce the chances to generate very short template answer just to get the rewards

takeaways.technique: Small clean expert-verified data beats mixed quality
takeaways.what_they_do: In science RL they found a small set of expert-verified high-quality questions outperformed a larger mixed-quality set.
takeaways.evidence_quote: a small blood clean data set gives much better performance

takeaways.what_they_do: Their vision model keeps original resolution and aspect ratio instead of squashing into a fixed square, which matters for screenshots and long vertical images.
takeaways.evidence_quote: keep the virtual input as original as possible ... instead of focusing everything into a fixed square
